fields.name: The Founding Edit
fields.description: KIRA's inaugural collection. Twelve foundational pieces built on the belief that restraint is the highest form of craft. Charcoal, midnight and ivory in wool so fine it moves like water.

fields.name: Milano Canvassed
fields.description: Full canvas construction. Milanese shoulders. The suit the way it was always meant to be made — built to last a lifetime and shaped to the body over years of wear.

fields.name: Chalk & Bone
fields.description: A study in light. Cream, chalk, warm ivory and bone — suiting for the warmer months that refuses to sacrifice structure for comfort.

fields.name: Black Label
fields.description: Evening and ceremony. Black barathea, midnight mohair, ivory marcella. Pieces made for the room you enter last and leave first.

fields.name: Savile Heritage
fields.description: An homage to the row. Traditional British cuts redrawn for a modern silhouette — the roll lapel, the hacking pocket, the suppressed waist.

fields.name: The Soft Tailoring Edit
fields.description: Structure you can forget you're wearing. Unlined. Unpadded. Unconstructed. The Italian art of looking effortless while being perfectly dressed.

fields.name: Atelier Separates
fields.description: Mix. Compose. Own your wardrobe. Blazers, trousers and waistcoats sold as individual pieces to build a wardrobe rather than a uniform.

fields.name: The Shirt Room
fields.description: Poplin. End-on-end. Sea island cotton. Dress shirts cut with enough generosity at the seat to tuck in cleanly and enough refinement to wear out.

fields.name: Cashmere & Merino
fields.description: Knitwear for the man who layers with intention. Grade-A cashmere and extra-fine merino in colours pulled from stone, fog and November light.

fields.name: Outerwear House
fields.description: Coats cut long enough to matter. Camel, charcoal and camel again. Wool-cashmere blends that improve with weather.

fields.name: The Accessories Room
fields.description: Ties. Pocket squares. Belts. Braces. The things that confirm a man's taste when the suit has already stated his intentions.

fields.name: KIRA x Bottega Pelle
fields.description: A limited collaboration with the Florentine atelier Bottega Pelle. Hand-stitched shoes and leather goods built to accompany a KIRA suit across decades.

fields.name: The Kira Two-Piece — Charcoal Herringbone
fields.description: Our signature two-piece in a 280g Super 120s charcoal herringbone. Full canvas chest, functioning button cuffs, notch lapel with a medium roll. The suit every KIRA wardrobe is built around.

fields.name: Milano Double-Breasted — Navy Pinstripe
fields.description: A six-on-two double-breasted in Super 130s navy with a discreet chalk pinstripe. Peak lapels. Milanese buttonhole. Full canvas. An unapologetically beautiful suit.

fields.name: Chalk Two-Piece — Ivory Fresco
fields.description: Cut from a Vitale Barberis Canonico fresco in warm ivory. Breathes superbly. A two-piece that handles summer heat without sacrificing a single line.

fields.name: Black Label Dinner Suit — Midnight Barathea
fields.description: Midnight barathea one-button peak lapel. Grosgrain facing on lapels and pocket welt. Matching barathea trouser with a single grosgrain braid. The KIRA tuxedo.

fields.name: Savile Three-Piece — Flannel Grey
fields.description: Mid-grey flannel three-piece. A hacking pocket on the jacket, side-adjusters on the trouser, a straight-cut waistcoat with five buttons. British tailoring precisely remembered.

fields.name: Soft Suit — Stone Linen Blend
fields.description: Unlined, unpadded, unstructured — the deconstructed suit for the man who dresses with ease. A linen-wool blend in warm stone. Patch pockets. No canvas, no compromise.

fields.name: Atelier Blazer — Charcoal Hopsack
fields.description: A blazer cut as a standalone piece — roomier in the chest, longer in the body, with patch pockets and a ticket pocket. Hopsack cloth. Works with denim or tailored trousers.

fields.name: Peak Lapel Blazer — Camel Doeskin
fields.description: Single-breasted peak lapel blazer in a camel doeskin. Structured shoulder, suppressed waist. The piece that does the most work in a wardrobe.

fields.name: Evening Jacket — White Duchesse
fields.description: The white dinner jacket. Duchesse weave, peak lapels, a single-button stance. Worn with the Black Label trouser or your own. For the occasions that demand a statement in white.

fields.name: Pleated Trouser — Charcoal Flannel
fields.description: A forward-pleated trouser with a generous cut through the thigh and a clean taper to the ankle. Side-adjusters, no belt loops. Charcoal flannel. The trouser that started arguments.

fields.name: Flat-Front Trouser — Navy Wool
fields.description: A clean flat front in mid-weight navy wool. Slim through the thigh, tapered to a neat ankle opening. Pairs with every KIRA blazer and most of life's situations.

fields.name: Linen Trouser — Warm Ecru
fields.description: Relaxed linen in warm ecru. A single forward pleat for comfort. Cropped slightly at the ankle. The summer trouser — works with or without a blazer.

fields.name: Cavalry Twill Trouser — Tobacco
fields.description: Cavalry twill in a warm tobacco. A slightly higher rise, side-adjusters, double-pleated. The country trouser that works equally well in the city.

fields.name: White Poplin — Spread Collar
fields.description: Two-ply Egyptian cotton poplin. A medium spread collar. Barrel cuffs. Cut with a clean tuck-in length and a slight suppression through the waist. The shirt every wardrobe begins with.

fields.name: Sea Island Cotton — Cutaway Collar
fields.description: Sea Island cotton end-on-end in a soft off-white. Wide cutaway collar. Double cuffs for links. The shirt you wear on the days that matter.

fields.name: End-on-End Blue — Tab Collar
fields.description: End-on-end weave in a cool sky blue. Tab collar — pins the collar beneath the knot, lifts the tie, sharpens everything. Classic double cuffs.

fields.name: Marcella Dress Shirt — Wing Collar
fields.description: Pique marcella front, wing collar, marcella double cuffs. For wearing with the Black Label dinner suit and nothing else. Perfection has only one context.

fields.name: Waistcoat — Charcoal Herringbone
fields.description: A five-button single-breasted waistcoat in charcoal herringbone, cut to companion the Kira Two-Piece or stand alone. Adjustable back strap. Welt pockets.

fields.name: Evening Waistcoat — Ivory Marcella
fields.description: Low-cut evening waistcoat in pique marcella. Single-breasted, four buttons. Worn with the Black Label dinner suit for a white-tie adjacency in black-tie company.

fields.name: Polo Coat — Camel Wool-Cashmere
fields.description: The polo coat. Double-breasted in a 70/30 wool-cashmere camel. Cut long. Patch pockets and a half-belt at the back. A coat that marks the decade it was bought in.

fields.name: Chesterfield — Charcoal Herringbone
fields.description: Single-breasted Chesterfield in charcoal herringbone. Velvet collar. Concealed fly front. Straight body, slightly suppressed. The most useful overcoat ever designed.

fields.name: Cashmere Crewneck — Oatmeal
fields.description: Grade-A two-ply cashmere in a warm oatmeal. Ribbed collar, cuffs and hem. The crewneck that layers under a blazer without breaking the line of the shoulder.

fields.name: Merino Rollneck — Charcoal
fields.description: Extra-fine merino rollneck in deep charcoal. The most versatile turtleneck in the range — under a suit, under a blazer, or alone. Wears without a tie and asks no questions.

fields.name: Cashmere V-Neck — Slate
fields.description: Grade-A cashmere V-neck in slate grey. Deep enough to show a collar and tie. The waistcoat alternative — and sometimes the waistcoat replacement.

fields.name: Silk Tie — Navy Repp Stripe
fields.description: Seven-fold silk tie in a navy and gold repp stripe. Woven in Como. 8.5cm blade width. The tie that always looks correct.

fields.name: Pocket Square — White Linen
fields.description: Irish linen pocket square. Hand-rolled edges. Brilliant white. The one square that never looks like it's trying.

fields.name: Silk Braces — Ivory with Gold Fittings
fields.description: Y-back silk braces in ivory with polished gold fittings and leather loops. Not for trouser waistbands — for trousers that already have buttons. The correct way.

fields.name: Oxford — Black Calf
fields.description: A plain-toe Goodyear-welted Oxford in black calfskin from the KIRA x Bottega Pelle collaboration. The shoe the suit has been waiting for.

fields.name: Derby — Dark Tan Grain
fields.description: An open-lacing Derby in dark tan grain leather. Goodyear-welted. The slightly more relaxed shoe — works with a blazer and trousers, or with the country suits.

fields.name: Leather Document Case — Black
fields.description: Full-grain black calfskin document case from KIRA x Bottega Pelle. Hand-stitched. Single interior partition and a document pocket. Carries everything. Shows nothing.

fields.title: Construction
fields.value: Full canvas chest piece, functioning button cuffs

fields.title: Origin
fields.value: Made in Italy — KIRA x Bottega Pelle

fields.title: The Maison Opens — Founding Edit
fields.description: Shot in the stairwells and salons of a 1920s Milan palazzo. The founding collection documented as a series of still lifes and figures — as if the clothes had always been there.

fields.title: Black & White — Black Label
fields.description: Evening only. A ballroom found empty in the early morning. The Black Label collection shot as if the party had just ended and the guests had been perfect.

fields.title: Country — Savile Heritage
fields.description: The English countryside as an idea more than a place. Fog on stone, dogs on gravel, three-pieces on men who look entirely comfortable in all of it.

fields.title: High Summer — Chalk & Bone
fields.description: Shot on a bleached terrace overlooking the Ligurian coast. The light-coloured suiting collection in its natural habitat — heat, aperitivo, architecture.

fields.title: The Atelier — Separates & Knitwear
fields.description: In the workrooms. Cloth on the table, light through tall windows, men dressed in pieces rather than suits — the separates collection as a study in composition.
